You are synthesizing a unified hypothesis from multiple parent hypotheses.
Goal: Can MVFA's segmentation adapters learn transferable localisation from image-level labels alone? Today they learn only from pixel masks of BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC. We replace the Dice and Focal seg_loss with a multiple-instance objective applied at all four levels to the segmentation-branch patch-to-text similarity map (mean of the top 2% patch anomaly probabilities; max and mean pooling as ablations), and train on all five source datasets with masks discarded. Primary question and hypothesis: because every patch is scored against a shared text anchor, image-level supervision aligns patch-level evidence with the text 'abnormal' direction, so the learned localisation transfers to the unseen modality and retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-level AUROC (with PRO and image AUROC also reported). A visual-only MIL control (same operator on a linear patch classifier without text anchors) tests whether text anchoring is responsible. Secondary analyses: per-level localisation quality, and a label-budget comparison on two held-out modalities between image-labelled training and mask-supervised training on 10%, 30% and 100% of the masked images.

Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):
- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.
- prompt.py / utils.py: the text side is two frozen text anchors (normal, abnormal) averaged over 35 templates.
- train_zero.py (zero-shot, leave-one-dataset-out): det branch trained with BCE on the MEAN-pooled patch anomaly map for every image; seg branch trained with Focal + Dice on pixel masks only for BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; batch size 1; the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- train_few.py: few-shot fine-tuning on K normal + K abnormal (masked) images from BMAD's valid/ split, one fixed draw (dataset/fewshot_seed); the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- test_few.py: zero-shot map (text similarity) and few-shot map (1 - max cosine to a memory bank of support patch features, per level) are each min-max normalised over the whole test set and added with weight 0.5; image score = max of fused pixel map (masked datasets) or mean-pooled det score (others).
- BMAD: BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC have masks; OCT17, ChestXray, HIS have image labels only; each has train/valid/test splits.

Required evaluation protocol: Shared evaluation protocol (from limitation group C: G2, G10, G12, G16): checkpoints and hyper-parameters are selected on a held-out validation split of the SOURCE modalities and never on the target test set, and the MVFA baseline is re-run under the same rule; results are reported under a modality-disjoint leave-one-modality-out split (RESC and OCT17 are held out together, never one with the other in training), with patient-level separation where identifiers exist, over at least 3 random seeds and 3 few-shot support draws with mean and standard deviation, and against the missing baselines named in G12 where relevant.
Parent hypotheses: Parent 1:
TITLE: Patch-level positive-unlabelled learning: normal-image patches as labelled negatives, abnormal-image patches as unlabelled
SUMMARY: Recast mask-free training of MVFA's segmentation adapters as positive-unlabelled (PU) learning at the patch level, using the non-negative PU risk estimator with a per-dataset class prior (expected lesion fraction) estimated from image-labelled data.
HYPOTHESIS: Non-negative PU learning with an estimated patch-level class prior retains at least 85% of mask-supervised MVFA's held-out pixel-AUROC margin over chance and outperforms asymmetric top-k MIL by at least 1.5 pixel-AUROC points, because it uses every patch of abnormal images rather than only the top-k.
RATIONALE: The parent's key insight — every patch of a normal image is normal — is exactly the labelled side of a PU problem: here the known class is 'normal' (labelled negatives) and abnormal images contribute an unlabelled mixture of normal and abnormal patches. PU learning theory gives an unbiased risk estimator for this setting once the mixture proportion (the fraction of anomalous patches in abnormal images) is known; MIL's top-k is a heuristic stand-in for that proportion. The proportion can be estimated without masks by mixture proportion estimation between normal-image and abnormal-image patch score distributions.
METHOD: 1) Patch classifier = MVFA's segmentation-branch patch-text logit z = t(cos(f, T_abn) - cos(f, T_nor)) + b. 2) Class prior pi_d for each source dataset d: mixture proportion estimation (best-bin estimator) on the zero-shot patch scores of normal vs abnormal images. 3) nnPU loss: with N = normal-image patches (labelled 'normal') and U = abnormal-image patches with mixing weight pi, R = (1 - pi) E_N[l(z, normal)]... implemented with the standard nnPU estimator (Kiryo et al.) where the negative class is labelled, max(0, ...) correction on the unlabelled term. 4) Sigmoid loss, lr 1e-4, 50 epochs; balanced batches of 4 normal + 4 abnormal images from the same dataset. 5) Code: loss.py nnpu_loss(); estimate_prior.py; train_zero.py.
EXPERIMENT: BMAD zero-shot leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); no source masks used by the proposed variants; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as reference; 3 seeds; pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Baselines: asymmetric SigLIP-MIL; top-k MIL; mask-supervised MVFA. Ablations: prior misspecification (x0.5, x2); estimated vs oracle prior (from masks, analysis only). Metrics: held-out pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC; prior estimation error (analysis). Falsification: no gain over asymmetric MIL.

Parent 2:
TITLE: Position-aware normal-bank pseudo-masks: matching each patch only to normal patches from the same anatomical neighbourhood
SUMMARY: Keep normal-bank pseudo-masks from image labels but substitute global nearest-neighbour search with a neighbourhood-restricted search over normal patches at the same grid position (+/- 2 patches), so anatomy that is normal elsewhere cannot hide an anomaly.
HYPOTHESIS: Position-aware matching raises pseudo-mask IoU by at least 0.08 over global kNN on BrainMRI and LiverCT training images (roughly spatially aligned) without reducing it on RESC, and the resulting segmentation adapters gain at least 2 held-out PRO points over global-kNN pseudo-masks.
RATIONALE: The parent's reviewed weakness is that global nearest-neighbour distances may fail for subtle medical anomalies: a lesion patch can resemble normal tissue from a different location (e.g. a hyperintense lesion resembling normal ventricles or skull), giving a small distance and a missed pseudo-mask. Brain MRI slices in BMAD come from co-registered volumes and liver CT slices are roughly centred, so restricting matches to the same spatial neighbourhood is a better normality model. The substitution keeps the parent's framing (image labels define normality, pseudo-masks supervise the segmentation branch) and its evaluation.
METHOD: 1) For each source dataset, store normal patch tokens per grid position (17x17) and level, coreset 20% per position. 2) For a patch at (u, v) of an abnormal image, distance = 1 - max cosine over bank tokens at positions within +/-2 in u and v. 3) Pseudo-mask = patches above the 99th percentile of the same score on held-out normal images of that dataset, foreground-restricted. 4) Datasets without spatial alignment (OCT17, ChestXray, HIS): a neighbourhood radius selected per dataset on its normal images (largest radius at which normal-vs-normal false positives stay below 1%). 5) Train segmentation adapters with Focal + Dice; code: make_bank_masks.py with position index.
EXPERIMENT: BMAD zero-shot leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); no source masks used by the proposed variants; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as reference; 3 seeds; pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Baselines: global kNN pseudo-masks (parent); mask-supervised MVFA; asymmetric MIL. Ablations: radius 0/1/2/4; coreset ratio. Metrics: pseudo-mask IoU per dataset (analysis), held-out pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC. Falsification: no IoU gain on BrainMRI and LiverCT.
